blocks.text: Models give a structured way to think about a problem and make complicated information easier to work with, which matters most in decision-making, where they let us consider different outcomes before choosing. A farmer can use a model of weather patterns and soil conditions to predict the best planting time and improve the chance of a good harvest.

blocks.prompt: Explain the role and importance of statistical models in solving real-world problems (long question 1).
blocks.explanation: A statistical model describes how variables are related, using past data, so it can explain patterns and predict new cases. It structures a complex situation (customers and earnings, study hours and results), lets us compare outcomes before acting (when to plant, how much to stock), quantifies uncertainty through errors and probabilities, and is tested on new data so decisions rest on evidence. Uses include weather forecasting, financial prediction, medicine and scientific research; models must also be fair and respect privacy.

items: Models structure complex information and let us compare outcomes before deciding (farmer's planting time).
